input.question: If the unreal engine is one of the most realistic and better looking game engines, why isn't it used more often in video games?
input.ground_truth: For indie dev: Game development is really, really hard already. If you don't need hyperrealistic graphics, why bother spending the extra hundreds of hours making detailed models, rigging them, creating animations, fine-tuning light sources, adjusting shader settings...? For established studios: Oftentimes, a studio will already have an engine they like to use, which they may have written themselves or bought from someplace else. Why bother learning a new engine and editor when you've already got experience with one that'll do the job fine? In general: It doesn't really make sense to say that the Unreal Engine, or any particular engine, is "one of the most realistic and better looking". That judgment is entirely subjective, not to mention massively in the developers' hands.

Okay, let’s imagine game engines are like different types of toy building blocks.

Unreal Engine is like a super fancy set of blocks that can build really pretty and cool castles. But even though these blocks are amazing and make beautiful castles, not everyone wants to use them.

Here’s why:

1. **They’re a little hard to use:** Some of the blocks are tricky and take a long time to learn how to put together. Not everyone has time to learn all the special tricks.

2. **They need a strong computer:** These fancy blocks are so big and detailed that you need a really strong computer to play with them. Some people’s computers can’t handle them.

3. **Other engines are easier or faster:** Some people want to build games quickly or make games that work on phones or small computers. Other block sets (like Unity) are easier and work better for those jobs.

4. **Cost and rules:** Sometimes, using Unreal Engine means you have to share some of your toys (give a part of your game’s money) to the people who made the blocks. Some people don’t want to do that.

So, even though Unreal Engine can make games look super cool, it’s not always the best choice for every game. People pick the blocks that fit what they want to build and what tools they have!
